topics.title: Management: Science, Theory and Practice
topics.definition: Management is the process of getting things done through people by planning, organising, staffing, leading and controlling.

children.title: Definition, nature and scope of management
children.definition: Management is both an art and a science, universal in application and concerned with results through others.

children.title: Levels of management
children.definition: Top level sets direction and policy, middle level translates policy into plans and supervisory level supervises daily work.

children.title: Managerial skills
children.definition: Technical, human and conceptual skills, with the mix changing by level.

children.title: Functions of management
children.definition: Planning, organising, staffing, directing, coordinating and controlling.

children.title: Management as a profession and its universality
children.definition: Growing professional standards, but management remains situational and practice based.

topics.title: Management and Society: Social Responsibility and Ethics
topics.definition: Management operates within society, so it must balance profit with obligations towards people and the environment.

children.title: Social responsibility of business
children.definition: Responsibilities towards employees, consumers, shareholders, government and the community.

children.title: Arguments for and against social responsibility
children.definition: Long run survival, public image and obligation versus cost, lack of skill and dilution of purpose.

children.title: Business ethics and ethical theories
children.definition: Utilitarian, rights and justice approaches to ethical decisions.

children.title: Values and ethics in the workplace
children.definition: Codes of conduct, whistle blowing, conflict of interest and ethical leadership.

children.title: Corporate governance and sustainability
children.definition: Board accountability, transparency, green practices and triple bottom line reporting.

topics.title: Nature and Purpose of Planning
topics.definition: Planning decides in advance what to do, how and when, so that goals are reached efficiently.

children.title: Nature of planning
children.definition: Primacy of planning among the functions, its contribution to purpose and its pervasiveness at all levels.

children.title: Types of plans
children.definition: Vision, mission, objectives, strategies, policies, procedures, rules, programmes, budgets and schedules.

children.title: Steps in planning
children.definition: Being aware of opportunities, setting objectives, developing premises, comparing alternatives, choosing a plan and implementing with review.

children.title: Management by objectives (MBO)
children.definition: Goal setting jointly with subordinates, action planning, review and appraisal against agreed objectives.

children.title: Obstacles to effective planning
children.definition: Uncertainty, lack of information, resistance to change, cost of planning and psychological barriers.

topics.title: Objectives and Planning Premises
topics.definition: Objectives are the ends towards which activity is aimed, and premises are the assumptions on which plans rest.

children.title: Nature of objectives and goal hierarchy
children.definition: Objectives form a hierarchy from socioeconomic purpose down to individual goals.

children.title: Setting objectives and SMART criteria
children.definition: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time bound objectives.

children.title: Management by objectives as a system
children.definition: Objectives, participation, feedback and performance review joined into a system.

children.title: Forecasting and planning premises
children.definition: Internal and external premises, with quantitative and qualitative forecasting techniques.

children.title: Vision, mission and values
children.definition: The long term aspiration, the purpose of the organisation and the beliefs that guide behaviour.

topics.title: Strategies, Policies and Strategic Planning
topics.definition: Strategy is the broad plan for achieving objectives by matching the organisation to its environment.

children.title: Strategic planning process
children.definition: Define mission, scan the environment, set objectives, generate alternatives, choose strategy and implement.

children.title: SWOT and environmental analysis
children.definition: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats analysed with internal and external scanning.

children.title: Porter generic strategies
children.definition: Cost leadership, differentiation and focus for competitive advantage, plus the value chain.

children.title: Porter five forces and the BCG matrix
children.definition: Industry attractiveness through competition, suppliers, buyers, substitutes and entrants; portfolio choices of stars, cash cows, question marks and dogs.

children.title: Growth, stability and retrenchment strategies
children.definition: Directions of strategy at corporate level, with diversification and vertical integration options.

children.title: Strategic versus tactical planning
children.definition: Strategy sets long term direction while tactics deal with short term methods.

topics.title: Decision Making
topics.definition: Decision making is the process of choosing among alternatives to reach an objective.

children.title: Types of decisions
children.definition: Programmed decisions follow rules for routine problems; non programmed decisions are novel and unstructured.

children.title: Rational decision making process
children.definition: Identify the problem, set criteria, allocate weights, develop and analyse alternatives, then choose and implement.

children.title: Bounded rationality and satisficing
children.definition: Real managers work with incomplete information and limited time, so they accept a good enough option.

children.title: Group decision making
children.definition: Brainstorming, nominal group technique and Delphi improve quality but may cause groupthink and slow decisions.

children.title: Decision trees and payoff tables
children.definition: Quantitative tools that show alternatives, states of nature, probabilities and expected values.

children.title: Creativity and innovation in decisions
children.definition: Encouraging new ideas and managing the risks that come with them.

topics.title: Nature and Purpose of Organising
topics.definition: Organising groups activities, assigns them to positions and defines authority so that plans can be implemented.

children.title: Organisation structure and design
children.definition: The formal pattern of relationships, and the choices of division of labour and coordination.

children.title: Formal and informal organisation
children.definition: The official structure versus the social network that emerges among employees.

children.title: Span of control and organisation levels
children.definition: The number of subordinates a manager can supervise, which decides how flat or tall the structure is.

children.title: Authority, responsibility and accountability
children.definition: Authority is the right to command, responsibility is the duty assigned and accountability is the obligation to report.

children.title: Delegation and its obstacles
children.definition: Transferring authority and tasks, with barriers such as fear of losing control on both sides.

topics.title: Departmentalization
topics.definition: Departmentalisation groups activities into manageable units so that common work sits together.

children.title: Functional departmentalization
children.definition: Grouping by work function such as marketing, production and finance, which gives expertise but slows coordination.

children.title: Product departmentalization
children.definition: Grouping by product line, which suits diversified companies with product managers.

children.title: Geographical departmentalization
children.definition: Grouping by territory, which suits sales and service organisations spread over regions.

children.title: Customer and process departmentalization
children.definition: Grouping by customer type or by production process step.

children.title: Matrix and team structures
children.definition: Employees report to both a functional and a project manager, which gives flexibility but creates dual authority.

topics.title: Line and Staff Authority, Decentralization
topics.definition: Line positions carry direct command responsibility while staff positions advise, and decentralisation spreads decision authority.

children.title: Line, staff and functional authority
children.definition: Line managers command operations, staff specialists support and functional authority lets staff give orders on narrow matters.

children.title: Line and staff conflicts
children.definition: Conflicts arise when staff advice is seen as interference or when line managers ignore expertise.

children.title: Centralization versus decentralization
children.definition: Centralisation keeps decisions with top management while decentralisation pushes them to lower levels, with degrees in between.

children.title: Advantages and disadvantages of decentralization
children.definition: Faster decisions, motivation and development of managers versus lost control, duplication and cost.

children.title: Recentralization and balance
children.definition: Technology and control systems allow partial recentralisation; the right balance depends on size and environment.

topics.title: Effective Organizing and Organizational Culture
topics.definition: Effective organising avoids structural errors, and culture shapes how people actually behave in the structure.

children.title: Avoiding organisational mistakes
children.definition: Eliminate unclear responsibility, flexible structures that confuse and over-complex delegation.

children.title: Ensuring flexibility and clarity
children.definition: Plans should be changeable, positions clearly defined and accountability traceable.

children.title: Organisational culture and its dimensions
children.definition: Shared values, beliefs and norms; dimensions such as outcome orientation, people orientation and team orientation.

children.title: Culture versus formal structure
children.definition: The structure says how things should work while culture decides how they actually work.

children.title: Learning organisation and knowledge management
children.definition: Encouraging continuous learning, systems thinking, teamwork and sharing of knowledge.

topics.title: Human Resource Management and Selection
topics.definition: HRM manages the people side of an organisation from recruitment to retirement.

children.title: Meaning, objectives and functions of HRM
children.definition: Acquiring, developing, motivating and retaining people to meet organisational goals.

children.title: HR planning and job analysis
children.definition: Forecasting needs and defining jobs through job description and job specification.

children.title: Recruitment sources
children.definition: Internal sources such as promotion and transfer; external sources such as advertisements, campus placement, agencies and referrals.

children.title: Selection process
children.definition: Application screening, tests, interviews, reference checks, medical examination and induction.

children.title: Types of tests and interviews
children.definition: Aptitude, achievement, personality and interest tests, and structured or panel interviews.

children.title: Orientation and placement
children.definition: Introducing the new employee to the organisation and fitting them to the right job.

topics.title: Training, Development and Performance Appraisal
topics.definition: Training builds skills for the current job while development prepares employees for future responsibilities.

children.title: Training methods
children.definition: On the job methods such as coaching, job rotation and apprenticeship; off the job methods such as lectures, case studies, vestibule training and computer based training.

children.title: Benefits of training
children.definition: Higher productivity, quality, morale and lower supervision need with fewer accidents.

children.title: Performance appraisal methods
children.definition: Rating scales, ranking, paired comparison, critical incident, essay, checklist, MBO based and 360 degree appraisal.

children.title: Appraisal problems and solutions
children.definition: Halo effect, leniency, central tendency and recency bias, reduced by training and objective criteria.

children.title: Career strategy and succession planning
children.definition: Career stages, career paths, mentoring and preparing successors for key posts.

topics.title: Manager and Organizational Development
topics.definition: Managerial development builds long term capability, and organisation development improves systems and culture.

children.title: Managerial development methods
children.definition: Understudy assignments, coaching, job rotation, special projects, committees and university programmes.

children.title: Learning and change
children.definition: Individual learning cycles and resistance to change, which must be managed openly.

children.title: Organizational development interventions
children.definition: Survey feedback, team building, sensitivity training, process consultation and intergroup development.

children.title: Organizational change models
children.definition: Lewin unfreezing, changing and refreezing model, and the role of change agents.

children.title: Employee engagement and retention
children.definition: Motivation, recognition, career growth and a healthy work environment to reduce attrition.

topics.title: Motivation
topics.definition: Motivation is the willingness to exert high levels of effort towards organisational goals.

children.title: Maslow hierarchy of needs
children.definition: Physiological, safety, social, esteem and self actualisation needs, satisfied from the bottom up.

children.title: Herzberg two factor theory
children.definition: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction while motivators such as achievement and growth create satisfaction.

children.title: McGregor theory X and theory Y
children.definition: Negative and positive assumptions about workers, which lead to different management styles.

children.title: McClelland three needs theory
children.definition: The needs for achievement, power and affiliation that drive behaviour.

children.title: Vroom expectancy theory
children.definition: Motivation equals expectancy times instrumentality times valence.

children.title: Equity and ERG theories
children.definition: Adams equity compares inputs and outcomes with others; Alderfer compresses Maslow into existence, relatedness and growth.

children.title: Motivation in practice
children.definition: Job enrichment, flexible work, recognition, fair pay and participative management.

topics.title: Leadership
topics.definition: Leadership is the ability to influence people to work willingly towards group goals.

children.title: Leadership versus management
children.definition: Managers rely on formal authority while leaders rely on influence and vision.

children.title: Trait and behavioural theories
children.definition: Early trait lists and the Ohio State and Michigan studies of consideration versus initiating structure.

children.title: Managerial grid and styles
children.definition: Blake and Mouton grid of concern for people and production, giving styles from impoverished to team management.

children.title: Contingency and situational theories
children.definition: Fiedler contingency model, Hersey and Blanchard situational leadership and path goal theory.

children.title: Transformational and transactional leadership
children.definition: Transactional exchanges rewards for performance while transformational inspires through vision and individual consideration.

children.title: Leadership skills and qualities
children.definition: Communication, decision making, empathy, integrity, courage and the ability to develop people.

topics.title: Communication in Management
topics.definition: Communication is the transfer and understanding of meaning, and it is the basis of all managerial work.

children.title: Communication process and channels
children.definition: Encoding, medium, decoding and feedback through formal and informal channels.

children.title: Downward, upward and lateral communication
children.definition: Instructions and policies flow down, reports and suggestions flow up, and coordination flows sideways.

children.title: Barriers to communication
children.definition: Semantic, psychological, organisational and personal barriers.

children.title: Grapevine and informal communication
children.definition: The informal network spreads information quickly, sometimes inaccurately, and can be used positively.

children.title: Effective communication and active listening
children.definition: Clarity, feedback, empathy, simple language and reducing noise.

children.title: Communication technology in management
children.definition: Email, video conferencing, collaboration tools and their effect on speed and richness of messages.

topics.title: The System and Process of Controlling
topics.definition: Controlling measures performance against standards and corrects deviations so that plans are achieved.

children.title: Control process steps
children.definition: Establish standards, measure performance, compare with standards and take corrective action.

children.title: Types of control
children.definition: Feedforward control before activity, concurrent control during it and feedback control after it.

children.title: Requirements for effective control
children.definition: Controls must be tailored, accurate, timely, economical and acceptable to the people involved.

children.title: Control and planning relationship
children.definition: Planning sets the standards that control measures, so controlling completes the cycle.

children.title: Critical point, control and management by exception
children.definition: Watch only the key deviations, which saves time and keeps attention on important matters.

topics.title: Control Techniques and Information Technology
topics.definition: Managers use budgets, ratios and information systems as control tools.

children.title: Budgetary control
children.definition: Expense, revenue, cash and capital budgets with variance analysis and flexible budgets.

children.title: Non budgetary control techniques
children.definition: Statistical data, break even analysis, ratio analysis, internal audit and personal observation.

children.title: Break even analysis
children.definition: Fixed and variable costs with contribution and margin of safety to find the no profit no loss point.

children.title: Management information systems
children.definition: Collecting, processing and reporting data for decision making and control.

children.title: Balanced scorecard and dashboards
children.definition: Measures across financial, customer, internal process and learning perspectives.

children.title: Information technology in control
children.definition: ERP, databases and analytics give faster, finer control but require data accuracy and security.

topics.title: Productivity and Operations Management
topics.definition: Productivity is the ratio of output to input, and operations management organises the processes that create value.

children.title: Measuring productivity
children.definition: Partial, multifactor and total productivity measures, and their use in comparing periods and units.

children.title: Quality concepts and TQM
children.definition: Fitness for purpose, continuous improvement, customer focus, employee involvement and statistical quality control.

children.title: Operations planning and control
children.definition: Forecasting demand, capacity planning, scheduling, inventory control and just in time.

children.title: Supply chain essentials
children.definition: Purchasing, logistics, vendor selection and the bullwhip effect in demand information.

children.title: Productivity improvement techniques
children.definition: Work study, method study, automation, training and better layout.

topics.title: Overall and Preventive Control, Toward a Unified Global Theory
topics.definition: Overall control looks at the total performance of the organisation while preventive control stops problems before they occur.

children.title: Overall performance control
children.definition: Financial controls through ROI and profit, plus comparative analysis and industry benchmarking.

children.title: Preventive control
children.definition: Managing by anticipation through good planning, selection, training and culture rather than after the fact.

children.title: Control pitfalls
children.definition: Over control, rigid standards and measures that encourage the wrong behaviour.

children.title: Systems and contingency approaches
children.definition: Viewing the organisation as an open system and adapting management style to the situation.

children.title: Global management and cultural dimensions
children.definition: Hofstede cultural dimensions, cross cultural leadership and managing multinational teams.

children.title: Management in the Indian context and the road ahead
children.definition: Joint family influence, jugaad innovation, family business structures and the shift to knowledge work and digitisation.
